questions.prompt: Which description best matches the government action discussed in the article?
options: It presents compulsory checks already operating on goods throughout the United Kingdom.
It proposes voluntary checks to replace the existing rules for timber products.
It announces a single new system starting across the United Kingdom in December.
It proposes checks in Great Britain alongside separate arrangements in Northern Ireland.
questions.explanationZh: 大不列颠正征询强制核查提议，并希望与北爱尔兰安排配合；不是全英国已经实行，也不是以自愿措施取代木材规则，12月日期只涉及北爱尔兰欧盟法规的分阶段适用。

questions.prompt: Why does the article mention toiletries and cosmetics?
options: To show that the forest risk extends beyond things people eat.
To explain why food companies need different regulations from shops.
To show that these products cause more forest loss than chocolate.
To explain why the government is changing product labels.
questions.explanationZh: s6说明相关原料也用于洗护用品和化妆品，风险不局限于食品；并未作数量比较或讨论标签。

questions.prompt: What does the article say about the 29,000 hectares?
options: It is the forest area that businesses expect to restore by 2030.
It is forest loss linked to UK consumption during 2023.
It is the area covered by new rules in Northern Ireland.
It is the forest loss recorded since the consultation opened.
questions.explanationZh: 这是与2023年英国消费相关的全球森林损失，不是恢复目标、法规面积或征询以来的损失。

questions.prompt: What difference between the two areas is described?
options: Great Britain has completed its changes, while Northern Ireland is consulting.
Both areas will introduce the same new regulations on 30 December.
Great Britain is consulting, while EU rules will start applying in Northern Ireland.
Northern Ireland has voluntary checks, while Great Britain has ended them.
questions.explanationZh: 大不列颠正在征询提议，北爱尔兰的欧盟法规将从12月30日起分阶段适用；不能将两套安排说成同一制度或已经完成。
